references.text: Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, formed an alliance against Gibeon, and this is the background for why the king of Jerusalem was defeated and listed among the conquered kings.
The five kings, including the king of Jerusalem and the king of Hebron, were brought out from the cave where they had hidden and later executed by Joshua.
Joshua captured Hebron and struck it with the sword, along with its king and all the towns belonging to it, as confirmed in the list of conquered kings.
Hebron is first mentioned as the place where Sarah died and Abraham purchased a burial site, highlighting the city's historical significance before it was taken by the Israelites.
The spies came to Hebron during the reconnaissance of the land of Canaan, demonstrating the city's strategic importance before the conquest.
Hebron was given to Caleb as an inheritance, confirming the conquest documented in the list of conquered kings.
